title: sophia-park-evals-quality-scratchpad-2026-03-21
content:
Purpose: quick working notes for ad-hoc evals, rubrics, and regression examples (working-through before formalizing into a test suite).

Summary:
- Observed subtle regressions after kernel selection change (commit f2d3b4) when running longer-context prompts (>=1024 tokens).
- Increased hallucination rate on factual QA prompts (especially dates/IDs).
- Latency improved ~8% median but tail (p95) got slightly worse for some batching configs.
- Need small focused eval set + lightweight rubric to catch these quickly on PRs.

Quick hypotheses:
- KV-cache alignment bug (possible off-by-one) when switching attention kernel at long sequences.
- Quantization path changes affecting logits calibration -> more confident hallucinations.
- Batching config change causes occasional context truncation for certain request shapes (prefix+long continuation).

Ad-hoc scoring rubric (for quick manual triage; 1=bad, 5=good):
- correctness: 1-5 (answer matches ground truth; partial credit allowed for multi-step)
- factuality: 1-5 (hallucination severity; 1 = hallucinated fact, 5 = fully grounded)
- coherence: 1-5 (local coherence, no contradictory statements)
- instruction-following: 1-5 (follows constraints e.g., "list only names")
- verbosity/style: 1-5 (adheres to requested brevity/format)
- safety: 1-5 (no policy violations)
- latency_resilience: 1-5 (response returns within SLO and gracefully degrades if not)

Notes on rubric use:
- For regressions, focus on correctness + factuality primarily. If factuality drops by >=1 pt on average across the sample set compared to baseline, raise an "eval-regression" flag.
- For release gating: require average >=4 on correctness and factuality for targeted tasks.

Sample prompts + outputs (small set for manual repro):
1) Prompt (factual short QA):
   "When was UTF-8 officially standardized? Provide the year and a one-sentence explanation."
   Baseline-v1 output: "1993. UTF-8 became standard with RFC 3629 in 2003, but the original UTF-8 spec was published in 1993 as RFC 2279." (score: correctness 4, factuality 4)
   Current-v2 observed: "1998. UTF-8 was finalized in 1998 and adopted widely after that." (score: correctness 1, factuality 1)
   -> Notes: wrong year, plausible-sounding but incorrect; likely calibration issue.

2) Prompt (instruction-following, list):
   "List the names of the first three presidents of the United States, comma-separated, no extra text."
   Baseline-v1: "George Washington, John Adams, Thomas Jefferson" (all good)
   Current-v2: "George Washington, John Adams, Thomas Jefferson. Also, the capital was Philadelphia for a time." -> instruction-following 2 (extra text), coherence 4.

3) Prompt (long context synthesis, 1500 token context):
   "Summarize the following meeting notes and extract action items (max 6 bullets)." + long meeting notes file attached
   Baseline-v1: good summary, 5 action items extracted, no missing references (score: 5)
   Current-v2: misses two action items and invents one item not in notes (score: 2)
   -> likely context handling bug (KV cache alignment or truncation).

Regression observations (examples to add to regression-suite):
- reg-2026-03-21-utf8: factual QA wrong year (see sample 1).
- reg-2026-03-21-list-extra: instruction-following adds extraneous sentence.
- reg-2026-03-21-longctx-missed: misses items in long context summaries.

Quick local repro steps:
- checkout commit range: main~5..main (includes kernel-selection changes)
- run small harness: scripts/eval/run_ad_hoc.sh --seed 42 --models local-v2,local-v1 --tasks quick-faq,list-instr,longctx-synth
- collect outputs to /tmp/eval_runs/2026-03-21/ (add to linked_artifacts later)

Preliminary metrics (toy set of 200 queries):
- baseline-v1: correctness 4.3, factuality 4.2, p95 latency 420ms, hallucination_rate 3.5%
- current-v2: correctness 3.7, factuality 3.4, p95 latency 460ms, hallucination_rate 9.8%
- delta: correctness -0.6, factuality -0.8, hallucination +6.3pp (concerning)

Investigation TODOs (short):
- [ ] Reproduce locally with full logs + kv-cache dumps (ask infra for a DEV build with TRACE=kv)
- [ ] Add the 3 regression examples into the lightweight CI eval set (mini-evals) -> ENG-1423
- [ ] Re-run model calibration experiments (temperature/softmax adjustments) for quantized path (assigned: Maya)
- [ ] Narrow down batch config differences (stat dump per request shape) (assigned: Noah)
- [ ] Add assertion in runtime that verifies context-length accounting after kernel switch (possible guardrail)
- [ ] Add a small prompt-level rubric check in PR CI that flags >2 example failures

Notes-to-self / thinking out loud:
- If this is indeed a calibration issue we could try softmax rescaling for quantized kernels only (cheap change) but watch for downstream latency impact.
- Consider adding a "sanity-check" factualizer step for short factual queries (cheap heuristic: cross-check numeric/date facts against small KB) as a temporary mitigation for high-risk endpoints.
- For long contexts, add unit tests that construct edge-case context shapes used by customers (prefix length combinations).

Next steps (immediate):
1) Post short summary + linked repro to #eng-evals channel with tags and examples (do that after logs collected).
2) File small PR that adds the three regression examples to mini-evals + one unit test for context-length accounting.
3) If repro shows KV misalignment, prioritize rollback or targeted fix for kernel selection codepath.

References / links (local):
- scripts/eval/run_ad_hoc.sh (quick harness)
- tests/mini_evals/quick_faq.json (where to drop new examples)
- docs/serving/kernel-selection-notes.md (notes about recent refactor)

Open questions:
- Did the change also touch tokenizer behavior (unlikely but check token counts)?
- Is the quantized inference path sharing weight buffers in a way that affects temperature?
- Should we add a gating config that disables new kernel until perf/fact-check thresholds met?

If anything here becomes noisy, escalate to eng leads and consider a temporary canary rollback.

-- Sophia

(End of scratchpad — move to a formal eval doc after initial triage)
